newsitem.title: UK: Gold edges higher in slow European trading.
newsitem.headline: Gold edges higher in slow European trading.

text.p: Gold prices drifted higher in quiet European trading on Monday morning but palladium was fixed sharply lower after coming under heavy selling.
Gold was fixed at $343.60 an ounce, up from Friday afternoon's fixing of $342.40.
Prices were expected to hold in a narrow range for the time being, due to the U.S. President's Day holiday, after managing a sizeable bounce up from 3-3/4 year lows last week.

"While the market is making a technical correction and further consolidation is a reasonable expectation today, there are few positive fundamentals around for the medium term," brokers GNI said in a report.

But palladium was fixed dramatically lower at $130.50 an ounce, compared to $136.25 on Friday afternoon. Prices have tumbled since then amid expectations that deadlocked talks between importer Japan and major producer Russia may begin soon.

Palladium had surged last week on speculative and consumer demand, hitting highs above $140 an ounce. But prices started coming off on Friday following news that the talks on supply contracts were likely to be revived in March, thereby easing supply tightness.

The market was battered further during Asian trading on Monday. Yen-based palladium futures on Tokyo's TOCOM futures market plunged by their daily limit of 22 yen per gram at the opening, depressed by lower spot prices.
"Whether it's speculative unwinding of positions or actual selling, it's having the same effect," a London dealer noted.
"The white metals seem to be leading the way. But with New York closed today I'm not expecting any fireworks in any of the metals -- just some position squaring," he added.
Platinum, following palladium's lead, also fixed $3.00 lower at $363.75 an ounce.
Silver was off Friday's New York highs, but still up four cents from the London close at $5.22/$5.24.
"Silver had a decent move up on Friday ahead of the Comex options expiry. Now it looks a bit toppy and without New York to support it it could drift lower," a dealer said.
But on the charts, silver was displaying buoyancy which could push it higher soon, some technical analysts said.

"Despite a still somewhat bearish background offered by the gold market -- with which silver normally correlates well -- impressive strength has come through here and it could be argued there is a serious attempt underway to form a base," said analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
